message.content: {"name":"end_turn","arguments":{"public_message":"Nothing for sale. Your move.","private_thought":"Cash $366, no monopoly on the board. No +EV trade: NY blocks p1 orange, Marvin blocks p2 yellow, Indiana blocks p3 red, States blocks p3 pink. Selling any hands a richer player a build path. Do not mortgage \u2014 next roll from Indiana can hit Atlantic $260 (2/3 yellow) or PA $320 (deny p2 green), and $366 covers either. Never trade NY to anyone who might flip it to p1. End turn."}}
message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am analyzing the board. I have four unmortgaged properties but no monopolies. Other players own many spaces.

I am the blocker king. I control New York Avenue and block p1's orange monopoly. I also control Marvin Gardens and block p2's yellow group. Several other properties remain unowned.

I also block p3's red and pink monopolies. I cannot build yet. I am weighing whether to trade or mortgage. I have enough cash to buy Kentucky or Atlantic. I am considering completing a set.

I mapped out the exact missing pieces for each set. Completing the orange, red, and yellow groups would require trading with p1 and p2 for unowned properties. I also noted that p3 owns Illinois and St Charles, which would help complete the red and pink monopolies.

I am now considering specific trades. p3 wants a full color set in exchange for Park Place, possibly to complete the dark blue group by taking Boardwalk from p2. I am also evaluating whether to trade Ventnor with p2 for a path to a monopoly.

I rejected trading New York Avenue. It is the most valuable property in the game. I also realized p2 cannot complete a yellow monopoly with just Ventnor and Marvin Gardens. I will not mortgage any of my properties.

I am now examining specific trade offers to p3. I could offer States Avenue or Indiana Avenue for Illinois. Indiana would help p3 complete their red group and would be a strong incentive.

I realized trading Indiana Avenue to p3 would complete their red monopoly and let them buy Kentucky. That is catastrophic. I also checked the yellow and dark blue paths. Both require giving away too much, and dark blue is too expensive to build with $366. Trading New York Avenue for light blue would hand p1 an orange monopoly. None of these trade paths look viable.

I checked whether buying Illinois or Ventnor from p3 and p2 would improve my position. They are too valuable to them as monopolies and blockers to sell for cash. No trade offers a clear advantage.

I am reconsidering p1's previous offer to trade New York Avenue for $300 and Electric Company. That would give p1 an orange monopoly with three houses, worth over five hundred dollars in rent per hit. I will not accept it.

I am now testing concrete trade offers. I considered proposing to p3 for Illinois in exchange for States and cash, but that would leave both of us needing unowned properties, and I might not afford Kentucky afterward. I also sketched a swap with p2: giving up Marvin Gardens for Ventnor plus cash.

I ruled out the swap with p2 because it would not change anything without cash. I also cannot acquire Park Place from p3 without giving up my only properties, which are single blockers. I will end the turn. I am now calculating possible landings from Indiana Avenue.

I mapped the spaces reachable from Indiana Avenue. I am already on that square, so the turn is over and no movement is possible. Post-turn actions are now the only options.

I will keep my public message simple and avoid telegraphing that I am blocking other players.

The most immediate threat is p2 landing on Pennsylvania Avenue for a green monopoly. They have over a thousand dollars and will likely buy it.

p3 and p2 could also form a dark blue monopoly if they trade Park Place and Boardwalk.

p1 needs Oriental Avenue to complete a light blue set, but that is less urgent than the green threat.

I mapped the exact buy priorities for my next roll from Indiana Avenue. Rolling a 3 lands on Atlantic Avenue, which I should purchase to complete the yellow group. Rolling an 11 lands on Pennsylvania Avenue, and I have enough cash to buy it and block p2's green monopoly. These two purchases are the most critical decisions.

I checked whether proposing a trade consumes the turn. Rejections happen immediately during the proposer's turn, so I could still take another action afterward. If accepted, the state updates right away.
